branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Program proceeds into a viable launch attempt within deadline.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Official readiness language shifts from window preservation to committed launch targeting and range allocation is locked.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Hardware checks close cleanly and safety review finds acceptable residual risk before end of March 2026.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Launch slips past March 31 despite continued intent to fly soon after.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: New engineering work, additional test cycles, or indefinite readiness wording appear in official updates.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: A material technical anomaly remains unresolved or emerges during final checks/rehearsal follow-up.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Mission remains broadly ready but misses deadline due to operational bottleneck.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Public references to recycled countdown infrastructure work, range conflicts, or narrowed attempt opportunities.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Ground system trouble or range unavailability compresses the final attempt window.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Launch readiness exists but mission scrubs into April, resolving no.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Official statements emphasize acceptable vehicle status while weather/red-rule conditions drive postponement.
branch_hypotheses.trigger: Weather constraints dominate near the final available pre-deadline opportunity.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Rollout and rehearsal are positive but do not themselves satisfy launch realization.
endpoint_ledger.description: Mission A2 physically launches on or before March 31, 2026 local launch-site time.
endpoint_ledger.label: Launch by deadline

meta.important_question: Does Mission A2 achieve an actual launch by March 31, 2026 local launch-site time?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the primary terminal yes endpoint defined by the scenario.
realization_criteria: Timestamp is on or before 2026-03-31 in local launch-site time
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Program is still attempting to preserve an early-2026 window, but multiple readiness-sensitive dependencies remain open.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A delay of less than 24 hours still realizes this endpoint if the launch occurs on April 1 or later.
endpoint_ledger.description: Mission A2 does not physically launch by March 31, 2026 local launch-site time, including launch on April 1 or later.
endpoint_ledger.label: No launch by deadline

meta.important_question: Are hardware and related technical checks closed in time to support a March 2026 launch attempt?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly defines this as the alternative terminal endpoint.
realization_criteria: No observable launch event by end of 2026-03-31 local launch-site time
OR first actual launch timestamp is 2026-04-01 or later local launch-site time
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Historical delays and multiple open sensitivity factors make deadline miss a live alternative at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Technical closure can occur without guaranteeing launch if weather or range causes a later miss.
endpoint_ledger.description: All material hardware and technical readiness issues are closed early enough to support a by-deadline launch attempt.
endpoint_ledger.label: Technical closure before deadline

meta.important_question: Does the crewed safety review process grant effective go-status before the deadline?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This endpoint-facing precursor distinguishes technical failure from nontechnical slip pathways.
realization_criteria: Official or authoritative readiness evidence indicates no material unresolved technical issue blocking launch before 2026-03-31
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Technical checks are explicitly listed as schedule-sensitive and crewed missions handle unresolved issues conservatively.

blockers: evidence that technical issues remained the primary blocker
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: If technical unresolved issues remain primary, this endpoint is not realized even if weather is also unfavorable.
endpoint_ledger.description: Mission becomes broadly technically and safety ready but still misses March 31 due to weather, range, or ground-system operational constraints.
endpoint_ledger.label: Operational miss despite readiness

meta.important_question: Do weather, ground systems, or range availability become the binding cause of a miss even if technical readiness improves?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Separates terminal no caused by operational timing from no caused by technical unreadiness.
realization_criteria: Authoritative evidence shows technical and safety readiness substantially achieved before deadline
AND no launch by 2026-03-31 due primarily to weather, range availability, or ground-system operational constraint
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Scenario explicitly includes weather, ground systems, and range availability as independent timing sensitivities.

risk_flags.note: Corpus does not name the actual organizations, launch site, or specific vehicle components; actors are therefore fictionalized and generalized.
Resolution is highly sensitive to local-time cutoff; even April 1 launch after short delay resolves no.
Crewed-flight safety review can dominate schedule logic and create abrupt slips from unresolved issues.
Prior delays imply latent skepticism and possible schedule fragility, but magnitude is not quantified.
Visible milestones like rollout and rehearsal may be misread as strong launch proof even though terminal criterion is actual launch by deadline.

simulation_brief.forecast_question: Will Mission A2 launch by March 31, 2026?
simulation_brief.primary_tension: deadline-constrained launch attempt versus conservative delay pressure from technical and operational readiness requirements
simulation_brief.summary: Mission A2 is a crewed lunar exploration mission following a prior uncrewed test. Vehicle rollout and rehearsal activity have occurred, but launch timing remains sensitive to hardware checks, ground systems, safety review, weather, and range availability. The program is attempting to preserve an early-2026 launch window after multiple historical delays.
uncertainty_notes: Exact launch provider, site, and organizations are unspecified in corpus.
No explicit current technical fault or weather issue is confirmed at T0.
Historical delays are referenced but not quantified.
Terminal evaluation is binary at the deadline boundary; launch on April 1 or later counts as no.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Observers update views from official milestones but also weight delay history.
Public attention likely spikes around launch dates, scrubs, and technical disclosures rather than at baseline.
Internal technical staff and crew are highly disciplined and unlikely to publicly express private concern.
Optimists and skeptics cluster around prior beliefs about schedule realism.
Single rumors may not dominate; repeated corroborating signals like scrub notes or successful tests matter more.
Program affiliation and enthusiast identity shape interpretation of delays versus caution.
Interest can fade between milestones but returns near deadline or launch attempt.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: A launch on April 1 or later counts as no even if delay is less than 24 hours.
Multiple historical delays bias observers toward skepticism about schedule commitments.
Safety and unresolved technical issues carry disproportionate decision weight for crewed missions.
Rollout and rehearsal create optimism signals without guaranteeing launch readiness.

trait_vectors.tendency: execute when systems and conditions align
